brief:
The way stories are told about wars shapes how societies understand conflict and violence, according to reporting on artists' commemorative practices. Acts of remembrance by artists defy dominant narratives that frame warfare through heroism and sacrifice, The Guardian reported.

These artistic interventions interrupt conventional war narratives by centering destruction and violence rather than martial glory. The work suggests that how conflicts are remembered and represented carries consequences for collective understanding of power and its relationship to armed conflict.
dek: Artists’ acts of remembrance about destruction and violence defy the dominant narratives of heroism and sacrifice The way stories are told about wars really matters.
title: Artists challenge war narratives through remembrance works
